page: Amazon Web Services x2gd.8xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and powered by AWS Graviton2 processors utilizing the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture. The instance exposes 32 physical cores mapped directly to 32 dedicated vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz, avoiding hyperthreading contention with exactly one thread per core. Memory allocation totals 512 GB, establishing an expansive 1:16 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 16 GB of RAM per core. The hardware configuration bundles 1900 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage alongside a 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The system contains no discrete GPU accelerators and incorporates 32 MB of Level 3 cache along with hardware-assisted AES cryptography.

Benchmark evaluations reflect the architectural profile of the Neoverse-N1 core layout. Multi-threaded processing reaches middle-tier industry ranges, evidenced by a multi-core Geekbench score of 11,488 and a multi-core stress-ng metric of 48,566.12. In-memory operations demonstrate stable throughput, registering 36.44 million Redis SET operations per second and average performance across PassMark database evaluations. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 139.81 GB/sec, while write operations achieve 70.12 GB/sec. Conversely, single-core metrics sit lower in comparative datasets, with a Geekbench single-core result of 942.0 and sub-optimal single-threaded compression speeds under gzip and bzip3 workloads. Similarly, small-model inference testing shows constrained token processing rates.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, x2gd.8xlarge yields high memory density per physical compute core, offering a cost-effective alternative to conventional x86 memory-heavy instances. The primary tradeoff lies in the balance between single-thread clock execution and total memory footprint, where high-throughput single-threaded tasks are constrained by the 2.5 GHz Arm cores. When configured for operations that require extensive memory buffering, massive key-value storage, or temporary local NVMe scratch space, the instance provides reliable operational isolation. It is best aligned with large Redis or Memcached clusters, in-memory databases, real-time analytics engines, and high-capacity caching layers.
description: Amazon Web Services x2gd.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by a 32-core AWS Graviton2 processor built on the arm64 Neoverse-N1 architecture at 2.5 GHz. Each vCPU maps to a dedicated physical core with 1.0 thread per core, backed by 32 MB of L3 cache and hardware AES encryption. With 512 GB of system memory, the instance delivers an expansive 1:16 vCPU-to-memory ratio, supplemented by 1900 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps. It contains no dedicated GPU hardware. Benchmark results place multi-core compute, static web serving throughput, and database operations within average industry distributions, achieving 36.44 million Redis SET operations per second, though single-threaded integer and compression performance remain relatively weak. The substantial memory footprint combined with direct NVMe instance storage positions x2gd.8xlarge for memory-heavy workloads, including in-memory key-value databases, real-time analytics engines, and large-scale data caching layers.
